What degraded

  • AN ITEM WAS ADMITTED FROM AN OFF LIMITS PATH AND HAS BEEN REMOVED. tx-2026-0126's three claims and its public access url all pointed at capitol.texas.gov/tlodocs/, which SOURCES_REGISTRY.md puts off limits in bold and which it warns is exactly the disallow a lowercase url reading routes around. No gate here compares a claim's host and path against that registry, so every check passed and a review bot on the pull request found it. The record went from 4 new items today to 3, and from 112 to 111. The gate that would have caught it is filed in the run record.
  • THE DECK NAMES ONE TEXAS PLACE AND IT IS THE WRONG ONE. Round Rock reached frame 6 and the caption on the fourth asking, out of the Horizon guide's own sentence about the successor's data center, and texan_check now reports a place where it reported none. It belongs to the SUCCESSOR and it is in Williamson County. The machine this deck is about sits at UT Austin in Travis County and is never located on any frame. The record knows the county and the deck could not print it, because none of the fetched sources say it. Worth saying plainly: the place was in a snapshot this run had already stored since 06:56, and three judges had to ask before anybody went and read it.
  • VARIETY IS THE DECK'S WEAKEST SCORE AND THE GATE CANNOT SEE WHY. The panel put variety at 6.0, well under everything else, and all three judges named the same cause: deck 14 on September 3rd was a Texas academic supercomputer whose own documentation restricts access, and the back half of this deck is a Texas academic supercomputer whose own documentation restricts access, four days later. dedupe_check returned 0.35 and cleared it, because it compares topic, entities and keywords and the entity lists share nothing. It is not a 30 day topic repeat by any fair reading. A reader following the feed still sees the same shelf twice in one week.
  • The scanner's daily ceiling was NOT checked. No Supabase connector is attached to this session, so the query could not be run at all.
  • Eight claims across two docket items now rest on publishers that exclude this project by name, seguingazette.com and newschannel10.com, so they can no longer be re-verified from here. The record says so on the items rather than quietly keeping the stamps.
  • Frame 6 is under its own plan. Its dossier specifies a shut containment door in two point oblique with a return wall giving a second value, and the render is a flat field, a light line and a latch box. craft_floor flags it as the deck's one quiet frame. It was not redrawn, because the scoring rounds were spent and a late redraw of the deck's turn is how a shipping deck turns red.
  • THE ASK INDEX IS 176 CHARACTERS UNDER ITS CEILING AND THAT IS NOT COMFORTABLE. CI failed on ask_pack at 40,082 against a ceiling of 40,000, and it passes now at 39,824 only because removing the off limits item gave back 258 characters. The index is the string every question in the box pays for, so the ceiling is a bill rather than a warning. Three or four more admitted items breaks it. The next run should expect to either shorten what each item contributes to the index or raise the ceiling deliberately, and it should not discover this from a red build.

Named here rather than left out. A run that quietly ships less than it planned teaches nobody anything.

Post this

Upload the PDF to LinkedIn as a document, title it Frontera's queues close October 1st, 2026, paste the post copy under it, then paste the first comment within a minute of posting.

carousel.pdf   contact sheet   the site

1. The post copy

Open science has a closing date.

The Texas Advanced Computing Center is switching Frontera off. Its own guide says the queues close permanently on October 1st, 2026. The same page calls it the largest cluster dedicated to open science in the United States. The guide's one promise for afterwards is that the file systems stay reachable. It never names a machine the work goes to.

The same center leads the construction project behind Horizon. That machine's own guide begins "This user guide is in progress". A dated notice says it is still limited only to internal users. Its guide says the machine is powered by a new 20 MW data center in Round Rock. The award runs to April 30th, 2028. One of the three ways in is the National Artificial Intelligence Research Resource Pilot.

A manual is how a public machine is open.

Where does the work go after October 1st, 2026?

#TACC #Frontera #NAIRR

The machine changed itself

  • `plan_render_check` compares the claim set every frame declares against every artifact that declares it: the dossier's `claims:` list, the dossier's `numerals:` sources, `copy.json`'s per-slide list, and the claim strip the frame actually prints.
    SLIDE_DOSSIER_SPEC.md line 19 defines `claims:` in six words, `every factual string on this slide, by claim id`, and until today nothing in this repository read that field at all. `dossier_check` does not mention it. On 2026-09-07 an integrity judge found three frames whose printed strip disagreed with the dossier that declared it, the run repaired those three, and the SAME judge came back the next round with two more, slide 3's labels and slide 8's numerals. That is the run's most transferable lesson happening twice in one hour.
  • `dedupe_check` counts and prints the BEAT of every deck inside its own window, joining each deck's `docket_item` to that item's `topic` in `ledger/docket.json`, and names the run at the head against the candidate's own beat.
    Deck 14 on 2026-09-03 was a Texas academic supercomputer whose own documentation restricts access. Deck 17, four days later, was a Texas academic supercomputer whose own documentation restricts access. Variety scored 6.0, the deck's weakest criterion, and all three judges named the same cause. This gate said faint. It was right on its own terms and structurally unable to be right: it compares topic, entities and keywords, and the two entity lists are disjoint, Texas A&M and Tarleton and TOP500 and NVIDIA against TACC and UT Austin and NSF and Frontera and Horizon. Two different machines at two different universities share no distinctive word. `topics.json`'s own `angle_note` field has complained about this blindness at decks 8, 11, 14 and 17, in prose, to nothing that could act on it.
  • `texan_check` reads the run's OWN FETCHED EVIDENCE, the snapshots in `sources/` as well as `claims.json`, and when the deck names no Texas place it names the places the evidence carries and the file each came from.
    Three judges charged carousel no. 17 for naming no Texas place. The run answered twice that no claim carried one. That answer was TRUE and it was about the wrong file: `claims.json` carried no place, and `out/2026-09-07/sources/horizon.txt`, a file this run stored at 06:56, reads `powered by a new 20 MW data center with advanced liquid cooling in Round Rock, Texas`, while both NSF award snapshots carry Austin. Nobody grepped the snapshots for four judging rounds. `no claim carries it` and `no source carries it` are different sentences and the second is the one a judge is asking about, because a claim is written by the run and a snapshot is what the world said.

Each reverts on its own commit.

This is a draft. Nothing was sent. The deck is already merged to main, so these links are live. Posting is the only step left, and it is yours.
